headline: Magnitude 7.1 earthquake near Hsinchu halts TSMC leading-edge fabs; advanced packaging lines offline
thesis: A quake near Hsinchu has idled TSMC's leading-edge lines and the CoWoS packaging that gates AI accelerator assembly. Valued as forward cash flow rather than price behaviour, almost all of the damage is timing: revenue deferred inside a disruption window, with only a small permanent share capitalised at each name's multiple. That is why the long-run portfolio impact is a fraction of the short-term move - the market prices panic in weeks, but only the permanently lost earnings survive to twelve months.

mechanism.effect: fabs evacuated and lines requalified, opening a multi-quarter allocation window rather than destroying capacity
the single-source step for AI accelerator assembly sets the pace of the entire downstream chain
revenue deferred out of the window, and a small permanent share of the AI socket capitalised at ~34x
a slipped capacity ramp against committed capex, hitting timing rather than the installed base
data-centre genset orders and grid interconnect demand defer with the build
a positioning rotation into defensives that carries no fundamental value and decays to zero by the long horizon

positions.rationale: Apple buys the leading-edge silicon for its autumn ramp from the idled lines, so a requalification window bleeds into a launch quarter. Almost all of it is timing: units deferred, not demand destroyed, which is why the permanent share is small.
positions.value_basis: market_cap_usd $3,450bn taken from the last close and cited; $210bn exposed revenue line x 42% affected x 9-month disruption window x 7.26% never recovered, at 26% margin, capitalised at 29x.
positions.variant_basis: low doubles the permanent share and lengthens the window (share moves to a rival roadmap); high assumes full catch-up inside the window with no lasting share loss. Band is +/-60% of base long-term, narrower nearer in.

citations.claim: Precedent, prior Taiwan quake: TSMC evacuated its fabs and suspended construction in the aftermath, and confirmed all personnel were safe.
Precedent, prior Taiwan quake: TSMC evacuated its factories in Taiwan following the earthquake.

Downside bound, prior Taiwan quake: TSMC's chipmaking facilities were rocked by the strongest quake in 27 years but escaped unharmed, its earthquake protection measures paying off. Evacuation does not imply structural damage, which is why this analysis capitalises only a small permanent share.
Seismic reference: magnitude, depth and epicentre data for earthquakes in the Taiwan region.
